content.text:
The pattern is CaMn2O4 (mvc-12108) alone. I simulated three candidates (CaMn2O4, TmNiO3 and KNaTi4(BiO6)2) and located peaks by grid index (2θ = 10 + 0.05 × index), not by fitting.

- **CaMn2O4 matches the peak sequence.** Its simulated peaks line up with the observed ones near 17.1°, about 28.2°, a doublet near 32.4/32.9° (the strongest peak), and the groups further up the scan.
- **Some intensities don't match.** The observed peaks near 17° and 28° are stronger than simulated (about 56 vs 37, and 30 vs 17). I put this down to preferred orientation or noise, not a second phase, but that is an inference.
- **The other two simulated candidates fit worse.** TmNiO3 has strong peaks that don't line up with the observed ones. KNaTi4(BiO6)2's strongest peak falls in a flat part of the observed pattern.
- **Not checked.** I did not simulate the remaining six candidates, so a minor second phase can't be fully ruled out.

{"present": ["mvc-12108"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "The CaMn2O4 simulated peak positions (about 17.1, 28.2, 32.4/32.9 degrees and higher-angle groups) line up with all major observed peaks, while TmNiO3 and KNaTi4(BiO6)2 fit worse and six candidates were not simulated."}
